the use of a 3T CMR protocol for patients with STEMI treated by primary PCI is feasible and safe, that the protocol provides high diagnostic accuracy, and that the protocol can be used in clinical practice for the diagnosis and assessment of myocardial infarct size and transmurality.

the infarct size and infarct transurality on CMR are significantly associated with infarct-related arterial patency and time-dependent transmurality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarctions treated by primary percu- taneous intervention.

1) the presence of a large infarct size, assessed by the transmural extent of infarction, is associated with the development of heart failure in patients with STEMI; 2) the extent of transmural infarction is related to the patency of the infraction-related artery and the amount of residual stenosis after PCI; and 3) a large infarction is associated with an increased risk of heart failure and death in STEMI patients.
